sentences.text: Dromomeron is a genus of avemetatarsalian archosaurs, a term meaning 'running femur', that lived between 220 and 211.9 million years ago.
Fossil remains, primarily hindlimbs, indicate that Dromomeron was about 1 meter long.
Specimens of D. romeri are interpreted as juveniles, limiting knowledge of the species' adult size and morphology.
The brain of D. gregorii features a floccular lobe of the cerebellum projecting into the semicircular canals, which are unusually large compared to other archosauromorphs.
The species D. gigas was described in 2016 from fossils found in the Quebrada del Barro Formation in northwestern Argentina.
The type species D. romeri is based on a complete left femur found at Hayden Quarry in Ghost Ranch, New Mexico.
The species name D. romeri honors the paleontologist Alfred Sherwood Romer.
The species D. gregorii is named after Joseph T. Gregory and is based on a right femur found at Otis Chalk Quarry in Texas.
The coexistence of Dromomeron with early dinosaurs like Chindesaurus suggests that dinosaurs did not immediately replace their archosaurian predecessors.
Dromomeron is classified in the clade Lagerpetonidae alongside the related genus Lagerpeton.
Dromomeron fossils are found in Late Triassic rocks in the Southwestern United States and northwestern Argentina.
Dromomeron lived during the Norian to Rhaetian stages, approximately 227.3 to 201.4 million years ago.

It is debated whether Dromomeron and Tawa hallae are the same species; Christopher Bennett proposed they were conspecific, but Rodrigo Muller rejected this in 2017 due to distinct femoral differences.
